summary: The bill requires HUD to limit sharing of any data collected from section 8 or public housing recipients to only verifying eligibility or benefit amounts, bars recipient agencies from other uses, and explicitly prohibits using the data for civil immigration enforcement.

scores.thoughts: The bill regulates data-sharing policies for HUD housing assistance programs but does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal expenditures. It imposes no new costs or savings on the government.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
The legislation concerns only housing assistance data and has no bearing on health insurance, providers, or coverage models.
No references to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations appear in the text.

Subsection (e) explicitly bars the use of collected housing-assistance data for civil immigration enforcement. This restricts information flow to immigration authorities and thereby expands privacy protections for non-citizens receiving HUD benefits.
The bill contains no language related to reproductive health services or abortion access.
No defense or military spending provisions are present.
Environmental regulation or climate policy is outside the scope of this data-privacy measure.

While the bill addresses data handling within HUD housing programs (a component of the safety net), it neither expands nor contracts benefit eligibility or funding levels; it only limits secondary uses of already-collected information.
No education funding, school-choice, or federal education policy provisions exist.
Drug enforcement or decriminalization is not addressed.
An exception is retained for ongoing criminal investigations, but the bill does not alter sentencing, policing practices, or rehabilitation programs.
Trade, tariffs, and globalization measures are absent.
The legislation has no fiscal impact on deficits or debt reduction strategies.
No provisions concern legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
Foreign assistance programs are not mentioned.
Voting access, voter ID, or election administration rules are outside the bill's scope.

The core purpose is to restrict the exchange of personally identifiable housing-assistance data except for narrowly defined eligibility purposes, thereby increasing privacy safeguards around government-held personal information.
Worker protections, union rights, and employer flexibility are not addressed.
No religious exemptions or anti-discrimination provisions are included.
